sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: This catalogue entry is greater stitchwort, Rabelera holostea (often called Stellaria holostea), a perennial of European woodland edges and hedges. Its brittle, ascending stems reach roughly 50 cm.

sections.title: Flowers and capsules
sections.text: Opposite, narrow leaves have rough margins. Spring flowers are about 2–3 cm across; each has five white petals split nearly to the middle, creating the appearance of ten. The ripe capsule opens by six teeth.

sections.title: Food
sections.text: A botanical study reports young aerial parts as edible, eaten raw or cooked; the plant is not treated here as a routine food. The illustration shows the deeply divided petals and rough-edged leaves used to recognize this species.
